summary: One high-severity error: the retained VS4 scope confuses compactness with the perfect-invariants criterion for ULA. A compact induction on the GL1 degree-zero stratum is an explicit counterexample. The family has complete layer coverage, valid supplier and link endpoints, and no dependency cycle after adjoining the proposal's links; the fifteen forwarding exceptions agree with the accepted review.

findings.claim: The proposal assigns VS4 'compact objects of finite HN support and perfect compact-open invariants'. The perfect-invariants requirement is false for compact objects and belongs to VS5's ULA criterion. It excludes the compact-induction generators the same VS4 contract imports from SR.2. The existing accepted VS4 compact-generation node and the original roadmap have the correct finite-support/compact-restriction criterion.
findings.evidence: Fargues-Scholze, Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence, https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/Geometrization.pdf, read 2026-10-01: Theorem V.4.1, printed p. 177, requires stratum restrictions to be 'compact, and zero for almost all b'; Theorem V.7.1, printed p. 183, assigns perfect open-pro-p invariants to ULA. Proposition VII.7.4 (p. 273) and Proposition VII.7.9 (p. 275) distinguish the same two properties for lisse coefficients. Explicit counterexample: E=Q_5, G=GL_1, H=Q_5^*, K=1+5Z_5 and Lambda=F_3. V=c-Ind_K^H Lambda=Lambda[H/K] is a compact projective smooth representation, since Hom_H(V,-)=(-)^K is exact and commutes with sums. H is abelian, so K acts trivially and V^K=V=F_3[Z x F_5^*] has infinite dimension; RGamma(K,V)=V[0] is not perfect over F_3. The degree-zero GL_1 stratum gives a compact, finitely supported Bun_G object violating the claimed invariants condition. See the report for the calculation and the existing node VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS4/compact-generation-and-compact-objects.
